domains.name: Beam
domains.description: Long intracellular helix running from beneath the distal blade to the pore module. The lever arm of the lever-like transduction mechanism: blade motion is transmitted along the beam to the anchor and thence to the inner helix.
domains.source: Zhao et al. Nature 2018 (PMID 30089899); Wang et al. Nat Commun 2018 (PMID 29610524)

domains.name: Beam coiled coil
domains.description: Coiled-coil segment at the distal end of the beam, annotated independently by UniProt in both species.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508/E2JF22 coiled-coil feature

domains.name: Piezo1.1 spliced segment
domains.description: The 24-residue segment removed in the Piezo1.1 splice isoform (PDB 6LQI). Identical in sequence between human and mouse, so the human deletion is 1388-1411.
domains.source: Geng et al. Neuron 2020, PDB 6LQI

domains.name: THU8 (TM29-TM32)
domains.description: Transmembrane helical unit 8 of the mechanosensory blade, comprising TM29-TM32. Proximal blade — resolved in cryo-EM.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508 transmembrane features, grouped in fours from the N-terminus

domains.name: THU9 (TM33-TM36)
domains.description: Transmembrane helical unit 9 of the mechanosensory blade, comprising TM33-TM36. Proximal blade — resolved in cryo-EM.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508 transmembrane features, grouped in fours from the N-terminus

domains.name: Anchor domain
domains.description: Amphipathic intracellular domain wedged between the blade and the pore module. Transmits beam motion to the outer helix. Its apex (human P2113/F2114) acts as a resistive brake on the inner helix; the same region also sits in a cholesterol/CRAC context.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508 topology; Li/Cox/Martinac Channels 2021; Buyan et al. Biophys J 2020 (PMID 32949489)
domains.rule: cytoplasmic topological domain between TM36 and TM37

domains.name: Elbow helices
domains.description: First layer of the helical cuff surrounding the pore at the level of the inner leaflet. Lies inside the anchor domain; named and delimited by Guo & MacKinnon, who argue the cuff is the part of the structure best placed to couple blade flattening to the gate.
domains.source: Guo & MacKinnon eLife 2017 (PMID 29231809), Results

domains.name: Base helix
domains.description: Second layer of the helical cuff, between the elbow and the hairpin. Inside the anchor domain.
domains.source: Guo & MacKinnon eLife 2017 (PMID 29231809), Results

domains.name: Outer helix (OH)
domains.description: Penultimate transmembrane helix; forms the outer wall of the pore module.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508 transmembrane features

domains.name: Cap / C-terminal extracellular domain (CED)
domains.description: Trimeric extracellular cap sitting above the pore, 234 residues per protomer. Contains the C2411-C2415 disulfide and carries the Er blood-group antigens. Rotates during gating and controls ion permeation through lateral portals.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508 topology; Karamatic Crew et al. Blood 2023
domains.rule: extracellular topological domain between TM37 and TM38

domains.name: Inner helix (IH, pore-lining)
domains.description: Final transmembrane helix. Three copies line the ion-conduction pathway and form the transmembrane gate.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508 transmembrane features

domains.name: C-terminal domain (CTD)
domains.description: Intracellular domain beneath the pore forming the cytoplasmic vestibule and the constriction that sets ion selectivity. Hosts the acidic residues controlling divalent permeation and most gain-of-function xerocytosis variants.
domains.source: UniProt Q92508 topology; Coste et al. Nature 2015 (PMID 26649819)

domains.name: Pore extension (PE) helix
domains.description: Helix continuing the conduction path below TM38 into the cytosol. Guo & MacKinnon name it and draw it in Figure 3a and Figure 6-figure supplement 1c,d — 'the pore, lined by TM38 and the PE helix' — but state no residue range for it anywhere, so this range is DERIVED, not quoted: the segment between the end of TM38 (mouse 2478) and the start of the hairpin (mouse 2501). The derivation is checked rather than asserted. Over that range in 6B3R every C-alpha lies within 11 A of the three-fold axis while descending 23 A along it, and the range contains E2487, H2490 and M2493 — the three residues the paper itself labels as constricting the pore there. A range that had picked up the hairpin instead would have C-alphas out at 20-34 A.
domains.source: Derived by rule from Guo & MacKinnon eLife 2017 (PMID 29231809): the pore-lining segment between TM38 and the hairpin. The paper names the helix; the boundaries are this project's.

domains.name: Hairpin helices
domains.description: Innermost layer of the cuff, contributed by the C-terminal domain of all three subunits. Inside the CTD.
domains.source: Guo & MacKinnon eLife 2017 (PMID 29231809), Results
